description: AIPE engineering rules V0 extracted from TI TIDA-010054 and Wolfspeed CGD15SG00D2, CGD1700HB2M-UNA, PRD-04814, PRD-06933 and PRD-09301. Rules from a single reference are never hard constraints; numerical limits carry an explicit basis; conflicting approaches are kept in 'conflicts'/'alternatives'.

categories.hard-constraint: Must hold for a correct and safe design; violation blocks release. Limits always cite their basis.
categories.optimization-objective: Quantity to minimise or maximise subject to the hard constraints.
categories.engineering-recommendation: Good practice with stated applicability; deviations need a documented reason.
categories.human-review-requirement: Cannot be decided automatically; a qualified engineer must review the stated item.

rules.title: Gate voltage within the selected device's absolute maximum
rules.statement: The steady-state gate rails plus their tolerance and the measured transient overshoot/undershoot at the device gate must stay inside the absolute-maximum V_GS range of the selected SiC MOSFET.

conditions: Any SiC MOSFET gate drive.

rules.rationale: Exceeding V_GS limits degrades gate-oxide lifetime and reliability; fast SiC transients can push the gate beyond the static rail values.

numerical_limits.parameter: Example absolute maximum V_GS (Wolfspeed Gen-3 C3M)
numerical_limits.basis: PRD-04814 §1; applies only to Wolfspeed 3rd-generation devices - use the selected device's datasheet

verification.procedure: Compare (rail + tolerance) and the worst V_GS excursion measured on the device side of R_G with an isolated probe against the datasheet absolute maxima.

rules.title: Independent turn-on and turn-off gate resistance
rules.statement: Provide separately tunable turn-on and turn-off gate resistance, using split driver outputs or steering diodes.

conditions: Hard-switched or partially hard-switched SiC positions where dv/dt, overshoot and switching loss must be balanced.

rules.rationale: Turn-on usually limits overshoot/EMI while turn-off can be faster; a single resistor forces the slower of the two values and raises losses.

verification.procedure: Double-pulse test sweeping R_G,ON and R_G,OFF; confirm V_DS overshoot and dv/dt limits.

alternatives.trade_off: No diode in the gate loop.

alternatives.approach: Turn-off steering diode with R_OFF in parallel (CGD15SG00D2)
alternatives.trade_off: Works with single-output drivers; diode drop and recovery affect the edge.

rules.title: Miller clamp or equivalent low-impedance off-state path when parasitic turn-on is plausible
rules.statement: Where complementary-switch dv/dt can lift the off-state gate (high R_G,OFF, long gate path, 0 V or small negative bias), provide an active Miller clamp or other low-impedance path to the turn-off rail, routed with low inductance to the device.

conditions: Half-bridge and bridge positions with high dv/dt.
exclusions: Designs with low R_G and low-inductance routing where Wolfspeed states the clamp is not strictly needed (PRD-09301 §5.8).

rules.rationale: Miller current through C_GD charges C_GS; a clamp bypasses the gate resistor during the off state.

verification.procedure: Measure V_GS of the off device during the complementary transition with and without the clamp (PRD-06933 §5 method).

conflicts.approach: Miller clamps are less effective for modules because the clamp path to the die is long

rules.title: DESAT trip level and blanking derived per design and measured
rules.statement: The overcurrent (DESAT) trip voltage and blanking time must be calculated for the selected device's V_DS(I_D, T_J) curve, the diode drops and the fault-risk tolerance, then verified in circuit; reference-design values must not be copied.

conditions: Gate drivers using V_DS desaturation detection.

rules.rationale: Trip current depends on R_DS(on) temperature; blanking trades false trips against short-circuit energy (PRD-09301 §5.1).

verification.procedure: Recompute with CB-GD-001 formulas, compare blanking + IC response with the device short-circuit withstand time, then measure trip behaviour.

conflicts.approach: TIDA-010054: 6.4 V trip with 1 us blanking (ZVS DAB, TO-247-4)
conflicts.trade_off: Fewer nuisance trips, more fault energy.

conflicts.approach: CGD1700HB2M-UNA: 6.7 V trip with ~46 ns external blanking + 120 ns IC deglitch
conflicts.trade_off: Fast protection; must be checked against ringing.

rules.title: Negative turn-off bias for half-bridge positions unless 0 V is justified
rules.statement: In half-bridge positions use a negative turn-off rail (Wolfspeed Gen-3: -2 V to -4 V, recommended -3 V to -4 V) unless switching tests show 0 V turn-off is acceptable for the device and layout.

conditions: Half bridges and bridges with high dv/dt.
exclusions: Single-ended topologies (buck, boost, flyback) where PRD-04814 states 0 V turn-off may be used.

rules.rationale: A negative rail adds margin against parasitic turn-on and speeds turn-off, while staying away from the negative V_GS limit.

verification.procedure: Measure off-state V_GS peaks during complementary switching for the chosen rail (PRD-06933 §4, PRD-09301 Figure 33 method).

conflicts.approach: Negative bias is not required for Wolfspeed devices; 0 V can be adopted after case-by-case evaluation
conflicts.trade_off: Simpler supply; heightened sensitivity to layout noise.

rules.title: BOM-configurable gate rails when multi-sourcing SiC devices
rules.statement: When more than one SiC supplier must be supported, lay out the gate-bias split network (and optional regulators) so V_GS levels can be changed by population options only.

conditions: Products with multi-sourced SiC MOSFETs having different recommended gate voltages.

rules.rationale: Different manufacturers and generations specify different V_GS; a configurable footprint avoids a PCB re-spin.

verification.procedure: Check that each supported device's recommended rails are reachable by documented population options.

rules.title: Gate-source discharge resistor on the device side of R_G
rules.statement: Fit a gate-source resistor directly at the device side of the gate resistor so the gate stays discharged when the driver is unpowered.

conditions: All SiC gate drives, particularly where the bus can be energised before the driver supply.

rules.rationale: Prevents charge build-up and unintended conduction while the driver is unpowered.

verification.procedure: Schematic and layout review: resistor present, between gate and Kelvin source, no component between it and the gate pin.

rules.title: Noise-immune gate-signal transmission
rules.statement: Transmit PWM and fault signals differentially (or by fibre) over cables and long distances, convert to single-ended as close as possible to the driver IC, and RC-filter every control and fault line at the receiving pin.

conditions: Gate drivers connected to the controller by cables or long traces in high-dv/dt environments.
exclusions: Short on-board links, where buffered single-ended PWM with RC filtering is acceptable (PRD-09301 §4.1; TI uses SN74LVC126A buffers).

rules.rationale: Single-ended references degrade over distance; differential pairs reject common-mode noise; the single-ended segment remains vulnerable.

verification.procedure: Inject or observe common-mode noise during switching; verify no spurious PWM/fault transitions; open-cable test keeps outputs off.

rules.title: Hardware interlock as last barrier, dead time from the controller
rules.statement: Cross-connect complementary PWM inputs (or add logic) so both switches of a leg cannot be on together, while still generating adequate dead time in the controller.

conditions: Half-bridge legs.

rules.rationale: Prevents shoot-through from controller faults or noise; interlock does not create dead time.

verification.procedure: Apply both PWM inputs high: both outputs must stay low; verify dead time at the gates.

rules.title: Review any external gate-source capacitor; avoid it on packages without Kelvin source
rules.statement: Flag every external gate-source capacitor for review; on SiC devices without a Kelvin-source pin (e.g. TO-247-3) Wolfspeed states it must not be used.

conditions: Gate circuits containing a capacitor from gate to source or Kelvin source.

rules.rationale: With a shared source path the capacitor can increase oscillation and overshoot; added C_GS also lengthens parasitic gate excursions.

verification.procedure: BOM/package check for three-lead devices plus review of any C_GS against the device datasheet and switching measurements.

alternatives.approach: Small capacitor or RC between gate and Kelvin source to reduce overshoot

rules.title: Soft shutdown on overcurrent; avoid two-level turn-off for modules
rules.statement: Turn the device off softly after an overcurrent detection (controlled-current or high-resistance path); do not use two-level turn-off with SiC power modules.

conditions: SiC positions with overcurrent detection, especially modules.

rules.rationale: Hard turn-off at fault current causes large V_DS overshoot; two-level turn-off concentrates stress (Spirito effect) per Wolfspeed.

verification.procedure: Short-circuit test measuring V_DS peak during fault turn-off.

rules.title: Do not rely on a gate-Kelvin Zener clamp for transient protection
rules.statement: Do not rely on a Zener from gate to Kelvin source to protect against fast gate transients; make the gate rails and layout robust instead.

conditions: Power-module gate drives.

rules.rationale: Zeners respond too slowly and are separated from the die by package inductance; useful only for steady-state clamping.

verification.procedure: Review any gate Zener's purpose; confirm transients are controlled by layout and rails (measure V_GS).

rules.title: Gate-bias power budget covers gate charge at the switching frequency
rules.statement: Each isolated gate supply must deliver at least the sum over its driven devices of Q_G * f_sw * (V_DD - V_EE), plus driver quiescent and any shared loads, within its rating at the actual input voltage and ambient, with margin.

conditions: All isolated gate-driver supplies, including shared supplies.

rules.rationale: Insufficient bias power collapses the rails, slows switching and can trigger UVLO or linear-region operation.

numerical_limits.basis: Charge Q_G is moved through the rail difference once per switching cycle (PRD-09301 Eq.1)

verification.procedure: Compute per supply with datasheet Q_G at the actual rails; compare with the supply rating; Wolfspeed applies margin (79 kHz -> ~70 kHz).

conflicts.approach: TI TIDA-010054 Eq.30 uses 2 * (V_DD - V_EE) * Q_G * f_sw, twice the Wolfspeed expression
conflicts.trade_off: More conservative; basis for the factor 2 not explained by TI.

rules.title: Common-mode choke at the bias-supply input, close to the converter
rules.statement: Where common-mode current through the bias supply is a concern, place a common-mode choke at the bias-converter input, physically close to the converter, with the converter's input capacitor between choke and converter.

conditions: Isolated gate-bias supplies on high-dv/dt switch positions.

rules.rationale: The choke raises the impedance of the common-mode path through the supply's isolation capacitance.

verification.procedure: Layout review of choke and capacitor order; optional EMI or common-mode current measurement.

evidence.location: sheet 2 L1 with C1/C2/C4 on converter side

rules.title: Minimise isolation capacitance of gate-bias supplies
rules.statement: Prefer bias supplies and transformers with low primary-to-secondary capacitance and estimate the common-mode current i = C_iso * dv/dt for each switch position.

conditions: High-side and fast-switching positions.

rules.rationale: SiC dv/dt drives current through isolation capacitance into control circuitry, causing noise and EMC problems.

verification.procedure: Compute i_CM from datasheet C_iso and the expected dv/dt; compare candidate supplies.

rules.title: Sharing a gate-bias supply requires review
rules.statement: Sharing one isolated supply between drivers referenced to the same node must be reviewed for circulating currents (decoupling resistors), combined power budget, symmetry of placement and source-referenced current-viewing resistors.

conditions: Low-side switches of inverters or totem-pole PFC sharing a reference.

rules.rationale: Shared references create circulating-current and coupling paths; one supply limits maximum switching frequency.

verification.procedure: Review layout symmetry, decoupling resistors and the combined power budget (KR-IS-001).

rules.title: Specify gate-rail regulation; post-regulate when precision is required
rules.statement: Specify the required gate-rail accuracy; unregulated module outputs suit many end applications, but use LDO or Zener post-regulation where characterisation-grade accuracy or non-standard levels are needed.

conditions: Isolated gate supplies.

rules.rationale: Rail tolerance shifts switching behaviour and V_GS margins; Wolfspeed recommends ±5 % rails.

verification.procedure: Measure rails across load and input range.

rules.title: DC-link capacitance from worst-case ripple charge
rules.statement: Size each DC-link capacitance as C >= dQ_max / dV_ripple,allowed, where dQ_max is the largest ripple charge over all operating corners (voltage ratio, power, modulation).

conditions: Converters with switched DC-link currents (DAB, PSFB, bridges).

rules.rationale: Ripple charge varies strongly with operating point; nominal-point sizing underestimates capacitance.

numerical_limits.basis: Charge balance on the capacitor over one ripple period

verification.procedure: Simulate or compute the capacitor current at every corner, integrate to dQ, apply the ripple limit.

rules.title: DC-link RMS ripple current within rating at frequency and temperature
rules.statement: The DC-link capacitor technology and quantity must carry the computed RMS ripple current at the switching frequency and worst-case temperature within the manufacturer rating.

conditions: All DC links with high-frequency ripple.

rules.rationale: Ripple current heats capacitors (ESR); film is selected for low ESR at switching frequency.

verification.procedure: Compute I_C,rms (e.g. TIDUES0 Eq.19 for DAB) and compare to datasheet ripple rating with frequency/temperature correction; measure case temperature.

rules.title: Bulk film plus distributed high-frequency ceramics at each bridge
rules.statement: Combine bulk film capacitance for energy and ripple with high-voltage ceramic capacitors distributed immediately beside each half-bridge to keep the high-frequency commutation loop small.

conditions: Board-mounted discrete SiC bridges at hundreds of volts.

rules.rationale: Film capacitors are physically large and far from the switches; local ceramics shorten the HF current loop (inferred from layout).

verification.procedure: Layout review of ceramic proximity to switch pins; extract commutation-loop area/inductance.

evidence.location: top overlay MLCC columns beside bridges

evidence.note: TI does not state the purpose; interpretation by AIPE

rules.title: DC-blocking capacitor sized well below resonance with the tank inductance
rules.statement: In transformer-coupled bridges susceptible to volt-second imbalance, add a series DC-blocking capacitor rated for full transformer RMS current and voltage, with C >= 100 / (4 pi^2 f_s^2 L) (series resonance a decade below f_s).

conditions: DAB or other bridges driving a transformer without inherent DC blocking.

rules.rationale: Mismatched PWM or driver delays can walk the transformer flux into saturation.

numerical_limits.basis: TIDUES0 Eq.20; equivalent to f_res <= f_s/10 (AIPE interpretation)

verification.procedure: Compute C_min and resonance; check RMS current rating; simulate switch-node waveform distortion.

rules.title: Isolated sensing parts rated for the system working voltage
rules.statement: Every sensor, isolated amplifier, modulator, isolated supply or other component that bridges an isolation barrier must have an isolation and working-voltage rating appropriate to the node voltage and the required insulation class.

conditions: Isolated voltage/current sensing and any barrier-crossing component.

rules.rationale: Under-rated barrier components defeat isolation and endanger the low-voltage side and operators.

numerical_limits.basis: Insulation coordination standard for the product (e.g. IEC 60664-1, UL 61800-5-1 named in PRD-09301 §2.7)

verification.procedure: Insulation coordination review: node voltage, working voltage (DC/RMS), required basic/reinforced class, datasheet ratings.

rules.title: Sensor scaling keeps worst-case signal inside the linear input range
rules.statement: Scale dividers and shunts so the maximum operating signal plus the required protection/overvoltage headroom stays within the sensor's linear input range.

conditions: All isolated voltage and current sensing chains.

rules.rationale: Clipping at full scale hides faults that protection must detect. Example (instance values, not targets): TIDA-010054 uses 1.57 V of a 2 V input, 0.76 V of ±1 V, and 37.5 mV / 30 mV of ±50 mV.

verification.procedure: Compute signal at maximum operating and trip levels; compare with datasheet linear range.

rules.title: Digital isolated sensing for long signal paths
rules.statement: Prefer an isolated delta-sigma bitstream (decoded by the MCU) over an analog signal when the sensing point is far from the controller.

conditions: Sensing points far from the controller; MCU with sigma-delta filter peripheral.

rules.rationale: A digital interface is less vulnerable to noise over long traces (TI).

verification.procedure: Review trace lengths and the MCU filter/clock configuration.

rules.title: Kelvin-connected shunts with filtering at the isolated input
rules.statement: Use four-terminal (Kelvin) shunt connections routed as a tight pair to an input RC filter at the isolated amplifier or modulator.

conditions: Shunt current sensing.

rules.rationale: Kelvin sensing excludes copper and solder drop from the measurement; the filter limits switching noise.

verification.procedure: Layout review of shunt sense pads and pair routing.

rules.title: Fast hardware path for switch-node overcurrent
rules.statement: Use a hardware overcurrent path (DESAT, fast comparator or a current sensor with built-in OC output) for switch-level protection; do not rely on ADC sampling in the control loop.

conditions: Switch-node and tank currents in fast SiC converters.

rules.rationale: Controller ADC paths need too many clock cycles relative to SiC short-circuit withstand times.

verification.procedure: Measure detection-to-PWM-off latency.

evidence.location: §3.3 Hall sensor chosen for low propagation delay

rules.title: Gate and Kelvin-source as adjacent-layer pours with Kelvin-source shielding
rules.statement: Route gate and Kelvin-source connections as wide pours on adjacent PCB layers, with the Kelvin-source layer between the gate and other circuitry.

conditions: Multilayer gate-driver PCBs for SiC devices.

rules.rationale: Adjacent layers give flux cancellation (largest gate-inductance reduction per Wolfspeed); the Kelvin layer shields the gate from noise.

verification.procedure: Check stack-up layer assignment and pour overlap for gate/KS nets; human review of layer images.
verification.aipe_hook: future extension of automation/verification/check_power_layout.py: per-net layer overlap metric

evidence.location: PCB Layout planes under related components

rules.title: Gate-driver decoupling inside the gate loop
rules.statement: Place the driver's positive and negative rail decoupling capacitors between the driver IC and the gate/source output, close to both, sized for the gate charge of the driven device(s).

conditions: All isolated gate drivers.

rules.rationale: The high-frequency gate current closes through the decoupling capacitors; their loop sets the effective gate inductance.

verification.procedure: Measure capacitor-to-driver-pin distance and loop area in the layout; check rail ripple during switching.

rules.title: Never tie the device Kelvin source to the power source in the layout
rules.statement: For devices with a dedicated Kelvin-source pin, the gate-driver return must connect only to the Kelvin-source pin; the PCB must not connect Kelvin-source and power-source nets.

conditions: SiC devices or modules with a Kelvin-source pin.

rules.rationale: An external connection reintroduces common-source inductance into the gate loop and can overload internal Kelvin bond wires.

verification.procedure: Netlist check that Kelvin-source and power-source nets are distinct and connected only through the device.
verification.aipe_hook: netlist rule: KS net must not share a net with S/power-source pins

rules.title: Prioritise power commutation loop inductance over gate loop inductance
rules.statement: Minimise the high-frequency power commutation loop first, then the gate loop; driver routing must not compromise the power loop.

conditions: Hard- and soft-switched SiC bridges.

rules.rationale: Power-loop inductance dominates overshoot and losses; gate-loop inductance matters but less (Wolfspeed).

verification.procedure: Extract commutation-loop geometry (capacitor-to-switch path) and compare alternatives; human review of overlays.

rules.title: Gate driver adjacent to its switch; minimise connector and probe-loop inductance
rules.statement: Place each gate driver (and its local decoupling) immediately beside its switch; for separate driver boards, mate as close as possible to the gate/source pins and provide a V_GS probe point at the device.

conditions: Board-mounted and plug-in gate drivers.

rules.rationale: Distance and connectors add gate-loop inductance, delay and noise pickup; connectors often dominate.

verification.procedure: Measure driver-to-device distance; check probe point location relative to R_G.

evidence.location: drivers on bottom side beside each TO-247-4

rules.title: High-current bus copper paralleled across layers
rules.statement: Carry DC-bus and bridge currents on wide pours repeated on several copper layers, stitched with via arrays, sized by a current-density/temperature-rise analysis.

conditions: Board-mounted power stages with tens of amperes.

rules.rationale: Parallel layers reduce resistance and inductance (inferred from observation).

verification.procedure: Compute copper cross-section and temperature rise; check via current capacity.

evidence.location: top, inner 1 and bottom power pours

rules.title: No copper crossing an isolation barrier on any layer
rules.statement: No copper (traces, pours, planes) on any layer may cross a gate-driver isolation barrier or the barrier between independently referenced driver channels; only components rated for the barrier may bridge it.

conditions: Isolated gate drivers, isolated supplies and isolated sensing.

rules.rationale: Copper across the barrier removes isolation, couples dv/dt noise and can damage the controller.

verification.procedure: Define keep-out zones per barrier and run DRC; inspect every copper layer image.
verification.aipe_hook: KiCad rule areas / keepouts per isolation barrier

rules.title: Creepage and clearance per standard for every net-class pair
rules.statement: Creepage and clearance between net groups must meet the applicable standard for the working voltage, pollution degree and material; nets connected to the drain through DESAT diodes carry full bus voltage.

conditions: All high-voltage PCBs.

rules.rationale: Arcing and tracking risk depends on voltage, surface and contamination.

numerical_limits.value: per applicable standard (e.g. UL 61800-5-1, IEC 60664-1, IPC-2221A)
numerical_limits.basis: PRD-09301 §2.7 names these standards; no universal value

verification.procedure: Derive distances from the governing standard; encode as KiCad net-class clearance rules; verify slots/cut-outs.

rules.title: Group nets of similar potential into spacing classes
rules.statement: Assign nets to spacing classes by reference potential (control/primary, each driver channel, DESAT midpoint, drain) so nets within a group route tightly while groups keep required spacing.

conditions: Isolated gate-driver and sensing layouts.

rules.rationale: Pins of one driver differ by ~20 V while groups differ by the bus voltage.

verification.procedure: Check every net has a class and class-pair clearance rules exist.
verification.aipe_hook: KiCad net classes and custom DRC rules

rules.title: Slots and cut-outs to extend creepage
rules.statement: Use board slots or cut-outs across isolation gaps when creepage, not clearance, is limiting.

conditions: Isolation gaps limited by surface creepage.

rules.rationale: A cut-out lengthens the surface path; clearance (through air) is unchanged.

verification.procedure: Measure creepage path around slots; confirm minimum slot width with the fabricator.

rules.title: Hardware short-circuit protection faster than device withstand time
rules.statement: Every SiC switch position in a product design must have hardware short-circuit/overcurrent protection whose total response (blanking + detection + soft turn-off) is shorter than the selected device's short-circuit withstand time under the actual conditions.

conditions: Product SiC converters.
exclusions: Evaluation fixtures where protection is provided externally (CGD15SG00D2 has no DESAT).

rules.rationale: SiC devices can fail within microseconds under short circuit; protection must act before failure.

numerical_limits.value: from the selected device datasheet or test

verification.procedure: Compute total response from driver datasheet and blanking; compare with device short-circuit data; verify by short-circuit test.

rules.title: Latched, combined fault reporting with UVLO lock-out
rules.statement: Hold outputs off during supply UVLO, latch overcurrent faults until an explicit reset, and report a combined fault to the controller.

conditions: Gate-driver subsystems.

rules.rationale: Reduced rails cause linear operation or false turn-on; a latched combined fault simplifies safe controller response.

verification.procedure: Fault-injection test of UVLO and OC paths, including reset timing.

rules.title: Protect the auxiliary input feeding bias supplies
rules.statement: Protect the auxiliary rail that feeds gate-bias supplies against reverse polarity and overvoltage (and, where practical, overcurrent/UVLO), with thresholds consistent with the bias converters' input range.

conditions: Auxiliary 12 V inputs to driver boards and power stages.

rules.rationale: A wiring fault on the auxiliary input can destroy all bias converters at once.

verification.procedure: Review thresholds against downstream input ratings.

rules.title: Device loss below the thermal-path limit at worst-case ambient
rules.statement: Each device's worst-case loss must be below P_max = (T_J,max - T_A,max) / R_th,total, where R_th,total includes junction-case, interface/insulation and the device's effective share of the heat-sink resistance.

conditions: Heat-sinked power semiconductors.

rules.rationale: Exceeding the junction limit reduces lifetime or destroys the device.

numerical_limits.basis: Device datasheet (TI used 150 degC for C3M parts)

verification.procedure: Compute with datasheet R_th,JC, measured or specified interface and sink resistances and maximum ambient; confirm by temperature measurement.

rules.title: Rated insulating interface for shared heat sinks
rules.statement: When several exposed-drain packages share a heat sink, use a rated insulating thermal interface and include its thermal resistance in the budget.

conditions: TO-247 class packages on common heat sinks.

rules.rationale: Exposed drains are at different potentials; insulation adds thermal resistance.

verification.procedure: Check interface voltage rating, creepage at the package edge and thermal resistance.

rules.title: NTC readings are not junction temperature
rules.statement: Treat module/board NTC readings as substrate or board temperature for cooling supervision; do not use them as junction-temperature protection without a validated thermal model, and isolate NTC feedback.

conditions: Designs using thermistor feedback from modules or heat sinks.

rules.rationale: Thermistor temperature differs substantially from junction temperature; module NTC isolation can fail after a catastrophic event.

verification.procedure: Review how firmware uses the temperature; calibrate the chain with a potentiometer.

rules.title: Verify soft-switching range across the operating envelope
rules.statement: For phase-shift-controlled converters, verify the ZVS boundary and RMS currents across the full voltage-ratio and load range, not only at the nominal point; plan modulation (e.g. EPS) where ZVS is lost.

conditions: DAB and related phase-shift converters.

rules.rationale: Away from unity voltage ratio and at light load, single-phase-shift loses ZVS and circulating current rises.

verification.procedure: Simulate the operating envelope; compare SPS and EPS losses.
